questions.question: A logged-in user requests an expense that belongs to another user. Which status code best describes 'authenticated, but not allowed'?
questions.explanation: 401 means the client is not authenticated; 403 means the server knows who the user is but refuses access. Some APIs return 404 instead to avoid revealing that the id exists.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent?
questions.explanation: Repeating a POST to a collection creates another resource each time. PUT, DELETE and GET leave the server in the same state however many times they are repeated.

questions.question: What should a successful POST /api/v1/expenses typically return?
options: 201 Created with the new resource and a Location header pointing to it
204 No Content with the new id in the body
202 Accepted with a redirect to the list
questions.explanation: 201 Created signals a new resource; the Location header gives its URL and the body usually contains the created representation. 204 must not have a body.

questions.question: How does an Idempotency-Key header make a payment POST safe to retry?
options: It makes Express convert the POST into a PUT
It encrypts the body so it cannot be replayed
The server stores the first response under the key and returns that same response for repeats instead of processing again
It tells the browser to cache the response for 24 hours
questions.explanation: The server records the outcome for each key; a retry with the same key replays the saved response, so the customer is not charged twice.
